# ui::WindowIcon

Header: `winui/ui/WindowShell.hpp`.

A small picture for the OS to show: the caption and taskbar icon, a taskbar overlay badge, or a thumbnail-toolbar button. It is one of three kinds, and the first one set wins:
- an image (straight-alpha RGBA), scaled to each size the OS needs
- a glyph drawn over an optional background, the same [IconGlyph](../rendering/icon-glyph.md) controls draw symbols with
- an icon from the app's own resources

Example: 
```cpp
// A glyph on the accent color as the caption/taskbar icon...
window.set_icon(ui::WindowIcon{.glyph      = ui::IconGlyph{0xE80F},
                            .foreground = ui::colors::White,
                            .background = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF0F6CBD)});
// ...and a red badge over the taskbar button.
window.set_taskbar_overlay(
    ui::WindowIcon{.glyph = ui::IconGlyph{0xE7E7}, .foreground = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFC42B1C)}, "3 unread");
```

## image

```cpp
Bitmap image {}
```

The picture, straight-alpha RGBA; takes precedence over [`glyph`](#glyph) when not empty.

## glyph

```cpp
IconGlyph glyph {0}
```

A Segoe Fluent Icons glyph, used when [`image`](#image) is empty; codepoint 0 is none.

## foreground

```cpp
std::optional<Color> foreground {}
```

The glyph's color. Unset draws it black on a light taskbar and white on a dark one, since the taskbar shows the icon, its overlay and the thumbnail buttons. It is redrawn when the user switches the taskbar's theme.

## background

```cpp
Color background = colors::Transparent
```

Filled behind the glyph; transparent leaves just the glyph.

## resource

```cpp
std::string resource {}
```

An icon the app ships with, used when [`image`](#image) and [`glyph`](#glyph) are both empty. It names an icon resource in the executable: `"APPICON"` by name, `"#101"` by number. It is loaded at each size the OS needs.

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

No image, glyph or resource: nothing to show.
